title: Cap. IX Resp. to Major's second confirmation: Christ obtained reconciliation for all — only individual impenitence bars participation
latin: Secundo contendunt neminem reprobari ut consideratum solummodo in communi Adae peccato, quia Christus omnibus reconciliationem impetravit, cujus ut fiant participes sola obstare potest impoenitentia singulorum. Ipsi solvunt nodum quem nexuerunt. Si enim ipsa Christi oblatione applicata reconciliatio sive redemtio omnibus et singulis esset obtenta, virium aliquid huic argumento inesset: sed sicut adultis non applicatur, nisi mediante fide et poenitentia actuali, ita neque infantibus nisi mediante Regeneratione supernaturali.
pass_a: Secondly they contend that no one is reprobated as considered only in the common sin of Adam, because Christ obtained reconciliation for all, of which that they may become partakers only the impenitence of singulars can stand in the way. They themselves untie the knot which they tied. For if by the very oblation of Christ applied, reconciliation or redemption were obtained for all and singular, some force would be in this argument: but as it is not applied to adults except by means of faith and actual penitence, so neither to infants except by means of supernatural Regeneration.
pass_b: Secondly they contend that no one is reprobated merely as lying in Adam's common sin, because Christ obtained reconciliation for all — and only each person's impenitence can bar them from sharing it. They untie the knot they tied. If reconciliation or redemption were obtained for every person by Christ's offering already applied, the argument would have some force. But as it is not applied to adults except through faith and actual penitence, so neither to infants except through supernatural regeneration.

title: Cap. IX Resp.: no promise of faith to every adult or regenerating covenant with every infant — passing over some in original sin alone is free right; Major not confirmed
latin: Jam quaero, Ubi Deus promisit se omnibus et singulis adultis praeparare velle et conferre illam fidem et poenitentiam, qua efficaciter et de facto reconcilientur Deo? Aut ubi foedus iniit cum infantibus universis, ut, non obstante originali peccato, teneatur eos pro reconciliatis habere, et supernaturali regeneratione in filios et haeredes vitae aeternae adoptare? Si hoc neque facit, neque facere tenetur, quosdam in solo originali peccato jacentes praeterit sive reprobat, neque in hoc agit injuste, sed libero suo jure utitur. Atque sic videtis, neque Majorem propositionem in se firmam fuisse, nec probationibus adjunctis solide confirmatam.
pass_a: Now I ask, Where did God promise that he wills to prepare and confer unto all and singular adults that faith and penitence by which they are efficaciously and in fact reconciled unto God? Or where did he enter a covenant with universal infants, that, original sin notwithstanding, he is bound to hold them for reconciled, and by supernatural regeneration to adopt them into sons and heirs of eternal life? If he neither does this, nor is bound to do it, he passes by or reprobates some lying in original sin alone, and in this he does not act unjustly, but uses his free right. And so you see that neither was the Major proposition firm in itself, nor solidly confirmed by the proofs annexed.
pass_b: Where, then, stands any promise that God will prep and confer on every adult the faith and penitence that actually reconcile them to him? And where has he bound himself by covenant to every infant — original sin or no — to count them reconciled and by supernatural regeneration make them sons and heirs of eternal life? He does neither, and owes neither. So when he passes over or reprobates some who lie in original sin alone, he wrongs no one; he exercises free right. The Major, therefore, was neither sound in itself nor made solid by the proofs they annexed.

lemmas.gloss: no universal promise of faith or infant regenerating covenant
passing over some in original sin alone is free right

title: Cap. IX Resp. to Minor: God reprobating those in original sin alone does not deal by strict or highest right
latin: Ad Minorem quod attinet, nego etiam et illud, Deum reprobantem stricto vel summo jure agere cum reprobis, si eos ut in solo originali peccato jacentes reprobet. Si summo jure ageret cum reprobis, simul ac in lucem editi essent, posset illos ut aeternae mortis reos in gehennam ablegare: Si stricto jure ageret, posset omnibus gratiae suae donis destituere.
pass_a: As to what pertains to the Minor, I deny also that, that God reprobating deals by strict or highest right with the reprobate, if he reprobate them as lying in original sin alone. If he dealt by highest right with the reprobate, as soon as they were brought forth into light, he could send them away into Gehenna as guilty of eternal death: If he dealt by strict right, he could destitute them of all the gifts of his grace.
pass_b: As for the Minor, I also deny that God, when he reprobates, deals with the reprobate by strict or highest right if he reprobates them as lying in original sin alone. If he dealt by highest right, as soon as they were born he could cast them into Gehenna as guilty of eternal death. If he dealt by strict right, he could strip them of all gifts of his grace.

lemmas.gloss: highest/strict right would allow immediate damnation or total destitution

title: Cap. IX Resp.: God confers corporal and spiritual benefits on the reprobate — therefore not strict right; false dichotomy with highest mercy
latin: At confert in eos subinde multa tum corporalia, tum spiritualia beneficia quibus reddantur meliores, et nihil quod illis debitum est subtrahit, nec illis infundit quicquam quo reddantur deteriores. Non igitur stricto jure agit cum illis. Sed adversarii ita hanc causam agunt, quasi inter haec duo, agere ex summa misericordia, et agere ex summo vel stricto jure, nihil esset medium.
pass_a: But he confers upon them from time to time many benefits both corporal and spiritual by which they may be made better, and he subtracts nothing that is owed them, nor does he pour into them anything whereby they may be made worse. Therefore he does not deal with them by strict right. But the adversaries so plead this cause as if between these two, to deal from highest mercy, and to deal from highest or strict right, there were no middle.
pass_b: But he often confers on them many corporal and spiritual benefits by which they may be made better; he withdraws nothing owed them, and pours into them nothing by which they are made worse. So he does not deal with them by strict right. Yet the adversaries plead as if between dealing from highest mercy and dealing from highest or strict right there were no middle.

lemmas.gloss: God still confers benefits on reprobates
false dichotomy: highest mercy vs strict right

title: Cap. IX Resp.: with the non-elect God acts from philanthropy, goodness, and admirable mildness — conscience convicts innate contagion or voluntary rebellion
latin: Fatemur Deum cum solis electis agere ex summa misericordia: sed affirmamus etiam, agere cum non-electis sive reprobatis non ex summo jure, sed ex φιλανθρωπία, bonitate ac lenitate admirabili; adeo ut convincantur in conscientiis suis se reprobationis decreto non fuisse a Deo impulsos, sed aut innata contagione aut voluntaria rebellione, aut utraque in mortem meritissimam incidisse.
pass_a: We confess that God deals with the elect alone from highest mercy: but we affirm also that he deals with the non-elect or reprobate not from highest right, but from philanthropy, goodness, and admirable mildness; so that they are convinced in their consciences that they were not driven by God by the decree of reprobation, but by innate contagion or voluntary rebellion, or by both, fell into most deserved death.
pass_b: Highest mercy, we grant, is how God deals with the elect alone. Toward the non-elect or reprobate his dealing is not highest right either, but philanthropy (φιλανθρωπία), goodness, and a mildness worth wonder. Their consciences themselves convict them: the reprobation decree did not shove them; innate contagion, voluntary rebellion, or both, brought them into a death they richly deserved.

lemmas.gloss: philanthropy toward non-elect, not highest right
conscience pins death on contagion/rebellion, not divine impulse

title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 open: God wills the saving grace of the Gospel offered promiscuously to all — Mat. 28:19; Mk 16:15; Col. 1:28
latin: Deus vult ut salutaris gratia Evangelii omnibus hominibus promiscue offeratur: quam suam voluntatem multis Scripturae locis patefecit, Matth. xxviii. 19, Euntes ergo docete omnes gentes, etc. Et Marc. xvi. 15. Euntes in mundum universum praedicate Evangelium omni creaturae. Hinc etiam Apostolus Coloss. i. 28. Nos annunciamus Christum, corripientes omnem hominem, et docentes omnem hominem, ut exhibeamus omnem hominem perfectum in Christo. Hic affectus Dei erga omnium hominum salutem, videtur arguere neminem ab eo fuisse reprobatum, nisi post considerationem gratiae contemtae, vel (quod eodem redit) nisi ex praevisione finalis infidelitatis et impoenitentiae.
pass_a: God wills that the saving grace of the Gospel be offered promiscuously unto all men: which his will he has opened in many places of Scripture, Matt. xxviii. 19, Go ye therefore and teach all nations, etc. And Mark xvi. 15. Go ye into all the world and preach the Gospel to every creature. Hence also the Apostle Col. i. 28. We announce Christ, warning every man, and teaching every man, that we may present every man perfect in Christ. This affection of God toward the salvation of all men seems to argue that no one was reprobated by him, except after consideration of grace contemned, or (which comes to the same) except from foresight of final unbelief and impenitence.
pass_b: God wills that the saving grace of the Gospel be offered to all men alike — a will he has opened in many Scriptures: Matt. 28:19, Go therefore and teach all nations; and Mark 16:15, Go into all the world and preach the Gospel to every creature. So also the Apostle, Col. 1:28: We announce Christ, warning every man and teaching every man, that we may present every man perfect in Christ. This regard of God for all men's salvation seems to argue that he reprobated no one except after regard to contempt of grace — or, what comes to the same, except from foresight of final unbelief and impenitence.

lemmas.gloss: Gospel grace offered promiscuously to all
adversaries: reprobation only after contempt / final unbelief
